\chapter{Circ\+Def}
\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef}{}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef}\index{CircDef@{CircDef}}
\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md9}%
\Hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md9}%
 \hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md10}{}\doxysection{\texorpdfstring{Introduction}{Introduction}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md10}
{\ttfamily Circ\+Def} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{CircDef_8swift}{Sources/\+Twos\+Cmplt/\+Circ\+Def.\+swift}}) is the decoded, in-\/memory representation of a Verilog-\/derived module\+: its declarations, parameter list, and a {\ttfamily Behav\+AST} describing every {\ttfamily assign}/{\ttfamily always}/{\ttfamily initial}/instance block found in the module\textquotesingle{}s YAML source. This page documents, in detail, how the right-\/hand side (RHS) of an assignment statement is parsed and turned into that representation, why {\ttfamily Circ\+Def.\+exprs} and {\ttfamily Circ\+Def.\+stmts} sometimes appear so lopsided (one full, the other empty) at a breakpoint, and evaluates a proposed algorithm for giving bit-\/slices and concatenation a real, structural presence in the simulated netlist.

This document was written as the first step of a staged effort (see {\ttfamily Claude\+Instructions.\+md} in the repository root) to fix how slices and concatenation are handled during circuit parsing and simulation. A handful of bugs found during this investigation were fixed alongside writing this document (all "{}known issue"{} sections below say explicitly whether the associated bug was fixed or left for a later pass); the larger structural change described in Part 2 is {\bfseries{not}} implemented yet and is left for a follow-\/up.\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md11}{}\doxysection{\texorpdfstring{Part 1 — How RHS assignment expressions are parsed today}{Part 1 — How RHS assignment expressions are parsed today}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md11}
\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md12}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{The two arenas\+: $<$tt$>$exprs$<$/tt$>$ and $<$tt$>$stmts$<$/tt$>$}{The two arenas: <tt>exprs</tt> and <tt>stmts</tt>}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md12}
{\ttfamily Circ\+Def} holds two independent, append-\/only arrays ({\ttfamily \doxylink{CircDef_8swift}{Circ\+Def.\+swift}\+:665-\/693})\+:


\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keyword}{public}\ mutating\ func\ internExpr(\_\ e:\ Expr)\ -\/>\ ExprId\ \{\ ...\ \}\ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ appends\ to\ exprs}}
\DoxyCodeLine{public\ mutating\ func\ internStmt(\_\ s:\ StmntAST)\ -\/>\ StmtId\ \{\ ...\ \}\ \textcolor{comment}{//\ appends\ to\ stmts}}
\DoxyCodeLine{public\ func\ getExpr(\_\ id:\ ExprId)\ -\/>\ Expr\ \{\ exprs[id.raw]\ \}}
\DoxyCodeLine{public\ func\ getStmt(\_\ id:\ StmtId)\ -\/>\ StmntAST\ \{\ stmts[id.raw]\ \}}

\end{DoxyCode}


{\ttfamily Expr\+Id}/{\ttfamily Stmt\+Id} are just wrapped integer indices into these arrays — bump allocators, not trees. {\ttfamily Stmnt\+AST} cases hold {\ttfamily Expr\+Id}s referencing into {\ttfamily exprs}; expressions never reference back into {\ttfamily stmts}. Every subexpression, including nested ones, gets its own entry in {\ttfamily exprs} — a single assignment with a 16-\/bit concatenation of single-\/bit selects (see below) can intern 30+ expression entries.\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md13}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Why $<$tt$>$stmts$<$/tt$>$ can be empty while $<$tt$>$exprs$<$/tt$>$ keeps growing}{Why <tt>stmts</tt> can be empty while <tt>exprs</tt> keeps growing}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md13}
This was the specific behavior observed at a debugger breakpoint that prompted this investigation, and it turns out to be by design, not a bug\+:

{\ttfamily Circ\+Def.\+stmts} is populated from exactly {\bfseries{one}} call site in the entire codebase\+: {\ttfamily Stmnt\+YAML.\+compile\+Stmt(in\+:)} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{CircuitParse_8swift}{Circuit\+Parse.\+swift}\+:1454-\/1482}), which is only reached while walking the body of a procedural block — {\ttfamily always}, {\ttfamily initial}, {\ttfamily if}, {\ttfamily case}, a loop, etc. Top-\/level {\bfseries{continuous}} {\ttfamily assign} statements never go through this path. Instead, {\ttfamily Assgn\+Blck\+YAML.\+to\+AST} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{CircuitParse_8swift}{Circuit\+Parse.\+swift}\+:1557-\/1567}) builds an {\ttfamily Assgn\+Blck\+AST} directly and hands it to {\ttfamily Circ\+Def.\+build\+Behav\+AST()} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{CircDef_8swift}{Circ\+Def.\+swift}\+:726-\/730}), which stores it straight into {\ttfamily Circ\+Def.\+behav} — {\ttfamily intern\+Stmt} is never called for it.

So a module built entirely out of continuous assigns (no procedural blocks) will have an empty {\ttfamily stmts} array for its whole lifetime, while {\ttfamily exprs} grows with every RHS subexpression from every assign. A concrete example already in the resource library\+: {\ttfamily Resources/\+Circuit\+Lib/\+M1\+M\+\_\+\+QDACCUM5.\+yml\+:826-\/898} is a continuous assign whose RHS concatenates {\ttfamily C1R} with sixteen single-\/bit selects of {\ttfamily ADDR1\+R\+\_\+} ({\ttfamily ADDR1\+R\+\_\+\mbox{[}15\mbox{]}} down to {\ttfamily ADDR1\+R\+\_\+\mbox{[}0\mbox{]}}) — each becomes its own interned {\ttfamily Expr.\+select}, but the whole statement never touches {\ttfamily stmts}.

This means "{}an assignment"{} is represented by two structurally different mechanisms depending on where it appears (continuous vs. procedural) — a real architectural wart, and the underlying reason {\ttfamily Assgn\+AST} needed to exist in more than one shape (see next section). It was left as-\/is in this pass; unifying continuous assigns and procedural single-\/assigns onto one storage path would be a reasonable follow-\/up but is a larger change than the scope here.\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md14}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{$<$tt$>$assgnst$<$/tt$>$ / $<$tt$>$concatst$<$/tt$>$, and why $<$tt$>$\+Assgn\+AST$<$/tt$>$/$<$tt$>$\+Single\+Concat\+AST$<$/tt$>$ were merged}{<tt>assgnst</tt> / <tt>concatst</tt>, and why <tt>AssgnAST</tt>/<tt>SingleConcatAST</tt> were merged}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md14}
{\ttfamily Stmnt\+AST} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{CircuitParse_8swift}{Circuit\+Parse.\+swift}\+:2235-\/2248}) has two cases for procedural assignment-\/like statements\+:


\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keywordflow}{case}\ assgnst(AssgnBody)\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ a\ single\ scalar-\/target\ procedural\ assign}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keywordflow}{case}\ concatst(ConcatStmntAST)\ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ an\ explicit\ multi-\/part\ /\ concat-\/target\ procedural\ assign}}

\end{DoxyCode}


These are not fully redundant in intent — {\ttfamily assgnst} represents one plain target, {\ttfamily concatst} represents a statement whose target was written as an explicit list of parts (e.\+g. a Verilog {\ttfamily \{a, b\} = x;}-\/style concat target) — but their backing structs, {\ttfamily Assgn\+AST} and {\ttfamily Single\+Concat\+AST}, were field-\/for-\/field identical\+:


\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keyword}{public}\ \textcolor{keyword}{struct\ }AssgnAST\ \{}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ \textcolor{keyword}{public}\ let\ lvalue:\ LValueAST}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ \textcolor{keyword}{public}\ var\ lwidth:\ Int\ =\ 1}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ \textcolor{keyword}{public}\ let\ rvalue:\ ExprId}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ \textcolor{keyword}{public}\ let\ delay:\ Double?}
\DoxyCodeLine{\}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keyword}{public}\ \textcolor{keyword}{struct\ }SingleConcatAST\ \{\ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ removed\ in\ this\ pass}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ \textcolor{keyword}{public}\ let\ lvalue:\ LValueAST}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ \textcolor{keyword}{public}\ let\ lwidth:\ Int\ =\ 1\ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ was\ \`{}let`,\ AssgnAST's\ was\ \`{}var`}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ \textcolor{keyword}{public}\ let\ rvalue:\ ExprId}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ \textcolor{keyword}{public}\ let\ delay:\ Double?}
\DoxyCodeLine{\}}

\end{DoxyCode}


Both were genuinely instantiated — {\ttfamily Assgn\+AST} via {\ttfamily Assgn\+Blck\+YAML.\+to\+AST} (continuous assign) and {\ttfamily Single\+Assgn\+YAML.\+to\+AST} (one per element of a procedural {\ttfamily Assgn\+Stmnt\+YAML.\+assgns} list), {\ttfamily Single\+Concat\+AST} via {\ttfamily Single\+Concat\+YAML.\+to\+AST} (one per element of a {\ttfamily Concat\+Stmnt\+YAML.\+concats} list). {\bfseries{Fixed in this pass}}\+: {\ttfamily Single\+Concat\+AST} was deleted; {\ttfamily Concat\+Stmnt\+AST.\+concats} now holds {\ttfamily \mbox{[}Assgn\+AST\mbox{]}} directly, and {\ttfamily Single\+Concat\+YAML.\+to\+AST} constructs an {\ttfamily Assgn\+AST}. {\ttfamily assgnst}/{\ttfamily concatst} were kept as two separate {\ttfamily Stmnt\+AST} cases, since they still represent a meaningfully different statement shape (one target vs. an explicit list of targets) even after the underlying per-\/part struct was unified.\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md15}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{The $<$tt$>$gen\+Assign\+Stmt$<$/tt$>$ dropped-\/lvalue bug (fixed)}{The <tt>genAssignStmt</tt> dropped-lvalue bug (fixed)}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md15}
The codegen consumer of {\ttfamily .assgnst} was {\ttfamily gen\+Assign\+Stmt} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Compile_8swift}{Compile.\+swift}\+:1010-\/1024}). Before this pass, it only handled {\ttfamily LValue\+AST.\+net}\+:


\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keywordflow}{if}\ \textcolor{keywordflow}{case}\ .net(let\ nd\_nm)\ =\ ast.lvalue\ \{}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ ctx.code.append(Instruction(op:\ .storeSignal(nd\_nm)))}
\DoxyCodeLine{\}\ \mbox{\hyperlink{Sim_8swift_a86f7c427338355ba7ee03ab0cf94632b}{else}}\ \{}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ print(\textcolor{stringliteral}{"{}Not\ a\ net\ name"{}})\ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ bitSelect/partSelect/indexedPartSelect/concat:\ silently\ emits\ nothing}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\}}

\end{DoxyCode}


Any procedural assignment whose target was a bit-\/select, part-\/select, indexed-\/part-\/select, or concat would silently produce no bytecode at all. By contrast, {\ttfamily .concatst}\textquotesingle{}s consumer, {\ttfamily gen\+Concat\+Stmt} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Compile_8swift}{Compile.\+swift}\+:1104-\/1111}), and the continuous-\/assign consumer, {\ttfamily gen\+Assgn\+Stmt\+Code} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Compile_8swift}{Compile.\+swift}\+:853-\/868}, used via {\ttfamily generate\+Assign\+Block}), both handle every lvalue kind correctly — {\ttfamily gen\+Assgn\+Stmt\+Code} does so by emitting a generic {\ttfamily .assgn(lvalue, delay)} opcode that the VM executes via {\ttfamily set\+Left\+Net} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Sim_8swift}{Sim.\+swift}\+:1255-\/1300}), which switches on every {\ttfamily LValue\+AST} case.

{\bfseries{Fixed in this pass}}\+: {\ttfamily gen\+Assign\+Stmt} now mirrors {\ttfamily gen\+Assgn\+Stmt\+Code} — it emits the same {\ttfamily .assgn(lvalue, delay)} opcode instead of a net-\/only special case, so it now correctly supports every lvalue kind via the already-\/proven {\ttfamily set\+Left\+Net} path, rather than adding a third independent (and error-\/prone) implementation of lvalue dispatch.

Note for future readers\+: as of this writing, {\bfseries{no YAML file anywhere in {\ttfamily Resources/\+Circuit\+Lib} actually uses {\ttfamily kind\+: assgnst} or {\ttfamily kind\+: concatst}}} (both are procedural-\/statement kinds; every procedural assignment in the current circuit library is written using {\ttfamily kind\+: blckst}/{\ttfamily noblckst} instead, i.\+e. plain blocking/non-\/blocking assignment statements, whose codegen — {\ttfamily gen\+Block\+Stmt\+Code}/{\ttfamily gen\+Non\+Block\+Stmt\+Code} — was never affected by this bug). So this was a live, real defect, but not one that has been silently corrupting any circuit in the current library; it\textquotesingle{}s now fixed regardless, and a regression test (see Verification below) exercises the previously-\/broken path directly.\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md16}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Slice/select expression representation}{Slice/select expression representation}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md16}
There is no dedicated slice/bit-\/select case in {\ttfamily Expr}/{\ttfamily Expr\+YAML} — every bit access, part-\/select, and identifier-\/with-\/bounds funnels into one case\+:


\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keywordflow}{case}\ select(name:\ String,\ args:\ [ExprId])\ \ \ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ Expr}}
\DoxyCodeLine{case\ select(name:\ String,\ args:\ [ExprYAML])\ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ ExprYAML}}

\end{DoxyCode}


The YAML {\ttfamily kind} tags {\ttfamily bit}, {\ttfamily slice}, and {\ttfamily ident} (when {\ttfamily ident} carries a non-\/empty {\ttfamily sgmnts} list) all decode into {\ttfamily .select} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{CircuitParse_8swift}{Circuit\+Parse.\+swift}\+: 157-\/208}). A single-\/index bit access ({\ttfamily ADDR1\+R\+\_\+\mbox{[}3\mbox{]}}) is normalized to a duplicated two-\/argument form ({\ttfamily \mbox{[}3, 3\mbox{]}}) at intern time ({\ttfamily \doxylink{CircuitParse_8swift}{Circuit\+Parse.\+swift}\+:472-\/476}, in {\ttfamily Expr\+YAML.\+to\+Expr\+Id}), so every downstream consumer of {\ttfamily Expr.\+select} can assume a uniform {\ttfamily (msb, lsb)} two-\/arg shape.\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md17}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{The $<$tt$>$kind\+: concat$<$/tt$>$ mis-\/decode in $<$tt$>$\+Expr\+YAML$<$/tt$>$ (fixed)}{The <tt>kind: concat</tt> mis-decode in <tt>ExprYAML</tt> (fixed)}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md17}
{\ttfamily Expr\+YAML} has its own proper {\ttfamily .concat(args\+: \mbox{[}\+Expr\+YAML\mbox{]})} case (used, for example, by {\ttfamily RValue\+YAML}\textquotesingle{}s handling of an {\ttfamily rvalue\+: \{ concats\+: \mbox{[}...\mbox{]} \}} block — see {\ttfamily M1\+M\+\_\+\+QDACCUM5.\+yml\+:830-\/898} above, which is the common, correctly-\/working shape for a concatenated RHS). Separately, {\ttfamily Expr\+YAML}\textquotesingle{}s own YAML {\ttfamily Kind} enum also declares a {\ttfamily .concat} tag ({\ttfamily kind\+: concat} with sibling keys {\ttfamily name\+:} + {\ttfamily concats\+:}), whose decode body was\+:


\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keywordflow}{case}\ .concat:}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ let\ name\ \ =\ \textcolor{keywordflow}{try}\ c.decode(String.self,\ forKey:\ .name)}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ let\ concats\ =\ try\ c.decode([ExprYAML].self,\ forKey:\ .concats)}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ self\ =\ .select(name:\ name,\ args:\ concats)\ \ \ \textcolor{comment}{//\ wrong:\ builds\ a\ .select,\ not\ a\ .concat}}

\end{DoxyCode}


This looks like a copy/paste error — it silently produced a {\ttfamily .select} expression carrying the concatenated parts as its {\ttfamily args}, instead of a {\ttfamily .concat} expression. {\bfseries{Investigated and fixed in this pass.}} A repo-\/wide search confirmed this exact shape ({\ttfamily kind\+: concat} at the {\ttfamily Expr\+YAML} level, i.\+e. inside an expression position, together with a {\ttfamily name\+:} key) does not occur anywhere in {\ttfamily Resources/\+Circuit\+Lib} today — every real {\ttfamily kind\+: concat} occurrence in the library (28 files) is a {\ttfamily Port\+Node\+YAML} value inside an {\ttfamily instance}\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily ports\+:} list (a structural gate/port-\/wiring context, decoded by a separate, unrelated, and already-\/correct decoder, {\ttfamily \doxylink{CircuitParse_8swift}{Circuit\+Parse.\+swift}\+:847-\/934}), and every real {\itshape expression}-\/level concat uses the untagged {\ttfamily \{ concats\+: \mbox{[}...\mbox{]} \}} shape handled directly by {\ttfamily RValue\+YAML}. So this bug was unreachable with current data — but it was still wrong, and trivial to fix correctly\+:


\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keywordflow}{case}\ .concat:}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ let\ concats\ =\ \textcolor{keywordflow}{try}\ c.decode([ExprYAML].\textcolor{keyword}{self},\ forKey:\ .concats)}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ self\ =\ .concat(args:\ concats)}

\end{DoxyCode}
\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md18}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{The tree-\/walking $<$tt$>$.\+select$<$/tt$>$ evaluator bug (fixed)}{The tree-walking <tt>.select</tt> evaluator bug (fixed)}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md18}
There are two independent evaluators for expressions, and — before this pass — they disagreed about {\ttfamily .select}\+:


\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item {\bfseries{Bytecode/\+VM path}} (used for continuous assigns and, via {\ttfamily gen\+Block\+Stmt\+Code}/{\ttfamily gen\+Non\+Block\+Stmt\+Code}, for {\ttfamily blckst}/{\ttfamily noblckst} statements)\+: {\ttfamily gen\+Expr}\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily .select} case ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Compile_8swift}{Compile.\+swift}\+:924-\/929}) emits a {\ttfamily .select(name, arg\+Count)} opcode, executed by the VM ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Sim_8swift}{Sim.\+swift}\+:1351-\/1372}) via {\ttfamily ctx.\+get\+Select(name, msb\+:, lsb\+:)} — correct.
\item {\bfseries{Tree-\/walking interpreter path}} (used by {\ttfamily eval\+Stmt}/{\ttfamily do\+Blckl\+Upd}/ {\ttfamily do\+No\+Blckl\+Upd} for statements reached via {\ttfamily .ifst}/{\ttfamily .whlst}/{\ttfamily .casest} bodies)\+: {\ttfamily eval\+Expr}\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily .select} case ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Compile_8swift}{Compile.\+swift}\+:247-\/249}) instead called {\ttfamily ctx.\+syscall("{}select\+\_\+\textbackslash{}(name)"{}, args\+:)}. {\ttfamily Context.\+syscall} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Sim_8swift}{Sim.\+swift}\+:766-\/778}) has no {\ttfamily "{}select\+\_\+"{}}-\/prefixed case and falls through to {\ttfamily default\+: return .int(-\/1)} — {\bfseries{any slice read evaluated through this path silently returned {\ttfamily -\/1}}} instead of the correct bits.
\end{DoxyItemize}

{\bfseries{Fixed in this pass}}\+: {\ttfamily eval\+Expr}\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily .select} case now evaluates its two arguments ({\ttfamily msb}, {\ttfamily lsb}) and calls {\ttfamily ctx.\+get\+Select(name, msb\+:, lsb\+:)} directly, matching the VM path\textquotesingle{}s already-\/correct behavior, instead of round-\/tripping through the syscall dispatcher.\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md19}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Write-\/side duplication (fixed in a later cleanup pass) and the $<$tt$>$gen\+Concat\+Stmt$<$/tt$>$ stack-\/discipline bug (fixed)}{Write-side duplication (fixed in a later cleanup pass) and the <tt>genConcatStmt</tt> stack-discipline bug (fixed)}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md19}
Writing to a slice/concat lvalue used to be implemented in two parallel, near-\/identical functions\+: {\ttfamily assign\+To\+LValue} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Sim_8swift}{Sim.\+swift}}, used by the tree-\/walking interpreter and by {\ttfamily gen\+Concat\+Stmt}) and {\ttfamily set\+Left\+Net} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Sim_8swift}{Sim.\+swift}}, used by the VM\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily .assgn}/{\ttfamily .blck\+Assign}/{\ttfamily .noblck\+Assign} opcodes). Both switched on every {\ttfamily LValue\+AST} case and did essentially the same bit-\/masking arithmetic against real circuit nodes ({\ttfamily ctx.\+circ!.set\+Node(...)}), and both were already correct — the duplication was in the arithmetic, not a bug.

There was a plain-\/text, non-\/compiled design note in the repository, {\ttfamily Sources/\+Twos\+Cmplt/\+Compose} (since deleted), that was worth understanding but was {\bfseries{not}} a description of this duplication — it quoted an older, already-\/superseded version of {\ttfamily assign\+To\+LValue} that wrote into {\ttfamily ctx.\+vars\+: \mbox{[}String\+: Value\mbox{]}} instead of a real circuit node. That was a legitimate concern about {\itshape that} older code, already resolved by the time this investigation started; {\ttfamily Compose} was deleted once this distinction was captured here, since its concern no longer applies to any current code.

{\bfseries{Fixed}}\+: the duplicated per-\/case bit-\/masking arithmetic ({\ttfamily .bit\+Select}/ {\ttfamily .part\+Select}/{\ttfamily .indexed\+Part\+Select}) was extracted into one shared private helper, {\ttfamily apply\+Slice\+Write(\+\_\+\+:val\+:upd\+Tm\+:ctx\+:)} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Sim_8swift}{Sim.\+swift}}), which both {\ttfamily assign\+To\+LValue} and {\ttfamily set\+Left\+Net} now call. The two public functions kept their own distinct contracts rather than being forced into one signature — {\ttfamily assign\+To\+LValue} takes an absolute timestamp and also advances {\ttfamily ctx.\+sim\+Time} as a side effect (used by the tree-\/walking interpreter and scheduled-\/update processing); {\ttfamily set\+Left\+Net} takes an optional delay relative to {\ttfamily ctx.\+sim\+Time} (used by the VM\textquotesingle{}s opcodes) and doesn\textquotesingle{}t touch {\ttfamily ctx.\+sim\+Time} itself. Unifying those two contracts would have been a real behavior change to core simulation timing, not a safe refactor, so only the genuinely-\/identical arithmetic was consolidated.

A second, independent bug was found in {\ttfamily gen\+Concat\+Stmt} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Compile_8swift}{Compile.\+swift}}), the consumer of {\ttfamily .concatst}\+: it called {\ttfamily gen\+Expr} (which only appends {\ttfamily Instruction}s to {\ttfamily ctx.\+code} during code generation — it never pushes onto {\ttfamily ctx.\+stack}, the array {\ttfamily Context.\+push}/{\ttfamily pop} operate on, which is only meaningfully populated later during actual VM execution) and then immediately called {\ttfamily ctx.\+pop()}, which had nothing to legitimately pop. {\bfseries{Fixed}}\+: {\ttfamily gen\+Concat\+Stmt} is now purely bytecode-\/emitting, mirroring {\ttfamily gen\+Assgn\+Stmt\+Code}/{\ttfamily gen\+Assign\+Stmt} — it emits a {\ttfamily .assgn} opcode per part instead of calling {\ttfamily assign\+To\+LValue} synchronously mid-\/codegen. As with {\ttfamily assgnst}/{\ttfamily concatst} themselves, no YAML file in {\ttfamily Resources/\+Circuit\+Lib} currently uses {\ttfamily kind\+: concatst}, so this was a real, confirmed, but dormant defect — a synthetic test ({\ttfamily test\+Gen\+Concat\+Stmt\+Writes\+All\+Parts}) exercises it directly since no production circuit does.\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md20}{}\doxysection{\texorpdfstring{Part 2 — Evaluating the proposed slice/concat-\/gate algorithm}{Part 2 — Evaluating the proposed slice/concat-gate algorithm}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md20}
The following six-\/point algorithm was proposed (see {\ttfamily Claude\+Instructions.\+md}) as a way to give bit-\/slices and concatenation a first-\/class, structural presence in the simulated netlist, rather than being purely a parsing/\+VM concept\+:


\begin{DoxyEnumerate}
\item Each assignment statement is realized in a Circuit using a concat gate.
\item Each concat gate has a single multi-\/bit output port.
\item The output of a concat gate goes to a simple node connected directly to one or more component input ports.
\item The input ports of concat gates come from {\ttfamily .slice} nodes; each input port comes from one {\ttfamily .slice} node.
\item The sum of the bit counts of all the {\ttfamily .slice} nodes must equal the bit count of the {\ttfamily .simple} node connected to the concat output.
\item Each concat is an async gate, included in sorting, and ends up in {\ttfamily eval\+Order}.
\end{DoxyEnumerate}\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md21}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Point-\/by-\/point evaluation against the current implementation}{Point-by-point evaluation against the current implementation}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md21}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item {\bfseries{Points 1-\/3}} already match the existing {\ttfamily .join} gate kind ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Gate_8swift}{Gate.\+swift}\+:158-\/171})\+: its {\ttfamily eval()} case loops over an arbitrary number of input nodes, shift-\/\+ORs each one in by its own bit width, and writes a single result to one output node — no truth table involved, and already arbitrary-\/width/arity (it\textquotesingle{}s used with 3 and 4 inputs today in {\ttfamily Resources/\+Circuit\+Lib/\+CNTR3.\+yml}/{\ttfamily CNTR4.\+yml}). No change to {\ttfamily .join} itself is needed to satisfy points 1-\/3.
\item {\bfseries{Point 4 is not true today.}} {\ttfamily .slice}-\/producing nodes exist (built via {\ttfamily add\+Seg}/{\ttfamily circ\+Seg}, {\ttfamily \doxylink{CircuitIO_8swift}{Circuit\+IO.\+swift}\+:24-\/60}, backed by the async {\ttfamily .seg} gate kind) but they commonly feed directly into an ordinary gate\textquotesingle{}s input — {\ttfamily in\+Port2\+Indxs}\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily .bus} case ({\ttfamily \doxylink{CircuitIO_8swift}{Circuit\+IO.\+swift}\+:62-\/102}) mixes {\ttfamily add\+Seg}-\/produced slice-\/node indices straight into a flat {\ttfamily inps} array used by whatever ordinary gate the port belongs to. There is also no {\ttfamily Nod.\+kind} field at all today — the {\ttfamily Nd\+Kind} enum ({\ttfamily .simple}/{\ttfamily .slice}, {\ttfamily \doxylink{Circuit_8swift}{Circuit.\+swift}\+:126-\/129}) that this proposal\textquotesingle{}s vocabulary matches is declared but completely unused anywhere in the codebase. Making point 4 true is genuinely new work, not a bug fix.
\item {\bfseries{Point 5}} is a simple, cheap invariant to assert wherever a concat gate\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily inps} list is assembled — not implemented yet since it depends on point 4 existing first.
\item {\bfseries{Point 6 is already true.}} {\ttfamily initialize\+Cmp\+Cnts}/{\ttfamily sort\+Cmp\+Refs} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Circuit_8swift}{Circuit.\+swift}\+:431-\/613}) never special-\/case {\ttfamily .join} or {\ttfamily .seg} — they get an ordinary {\ttfamily Cmp\+Ref(kind\+: .a\+Circ, ...)}, are ref-\/counted like any other async gate, and are evaluated in the normal {\ttfamily eval\+Order} loop. The scheduler needs no changes to support this proposal.
\end{DoxyItemize}\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md22}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Comparison with other simulators, and a recommendation}{Comparison with other simulators, and a recommendation}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md22}
Mainstream Verilog tools (Icarus Verilog, Verilator) generally do {\bfseries{not}} reify every bit-\/select/concat as its own structural cell in the general case — a purely combinational, constant-\/indexed {\ttfamily \{a, b\mbox{[}3\+:0\mbox{]}, c\}} is typically folded into one expression-\/level "{}select-\/and-\/merge"{} operation at compile time, since (from a synthesis/simulation-\/performance point of view) a plain value-\/level bit manipulation has no observable timing difference from a physical concat cell, and reifying one for every small select would explode gate/node counts for circuits like {\ttfamily M1\+M\+\_\+\+QDACCUM5} (sixteen single-\/bit selects in one assignment).

That comparison, however, is optimizing for a different goal than this project has. This simulator\textquotesingle{}s central purpose is exposing a real, waveform-\/inspectable structural netlist (VCD output via {\ttfamily Glbls.\+node\+Chngs}) — being able to individually name and probe a slice node in a waveform viewer has direct value here that a synthesis-\/focused tool\textquotesingle{}s compiler pass doesn\textquotesingle{}t care about. {\bfseries{Recommendation\+: adopt the proposed algorithm}}, scoped specifically to Verilog-\/derived assignment statements, where there is a real gap to close today — those statements currently produce {\bfseries{no netlist-\/level representation of concatenation at all}}. Concatenation there is purely a bytecode-\/\+VM value operation ({\ttfamily Two\+Cmplt.\+join\+Bts}, driving the {\ttfamily .concat} opcode, {\ttfamily \doxylink{Sim_8swift}{Sim.\+swift}} \texorpdfstring{$\sim$}{\string~}1290+), invisible to VCD output and to anything that walks the structural netlist. The existing gate-\/level {\ttfamily .join} mechanism (used today only by the native, non-\/\+Verilog {\ttfamily CNTR3.\+yml}/{\ttfamily CNTR4.\+yml}-\/style circuit YAML) is exactly the right building block to reuse for this — it should remain a single, separate mechanism from the VM-\/internal {\ttfamily join\+Bts} path, not be merged with it; the two serve different layers (structural netlist vs. procedural expression evaluation) and conflating them would be a mistake.

One open design question this document originally surfaced without resolving\+: should {\bfseries{every}} slice always get its own concat gate, even when a port is fed by exactly one slice (the literal reading of point 4), or only when a port\textquotesingle{}s connection is a genuine concatenation of two or more slices (avoiding a degenerate one-\/input "{}concat"{} gate for the common single-\/bit-\/ select case)? {\bfseries{Resolved\+: the latter ("{}\+Option B"{}).}} A port fed by exactly one slice wires that slice directly, with no gate in between; a port fed by two or more slices gets a real {\ttfamily .join} gate concatenating them.\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md23}{}\doxysection{\texorpdfstring{Part 3 — What was actually implemented, and what wasn\textquotesingle{}t}{Part 3 — What was actually implemented, and what wasn't}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md23}
Two follow-\/up investigations narrowed Part 2\textquotesingle{}s recommendation further before any code was written\+:


\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item {\bfseries{Verilog-\/derived circuits were excluded from this work entirely.}} Making Verilog-\/derived {\ttfamily assign}/{\ttfamily always} bodies produce real structural nodes/gates would require inventing a new structural execution model for that whole subsystem — today, {\itshape nothing} about their behavior is structural (not just concatenation; every expression, binary op, and conditional is opaque bytecode run by the VM each timestep, invisible to {\ttfamily eval\+Order}). That\textquotesingle{}s a much larger project than "{}add slice/concat gates,"{} so it was deliberately left out of scope. Only the native gate-\/level format ({\ttfamily kind\+: subcirc} YAML, built via {\ttfamily Circuit.\+make}/{\ttfamily Make\+Circuit} in {\ttfamily \doxylink{CircuitIO_8swift}{Circuit\+IO.\+swift}}) has any structural representation to retrofit at all.
\item {\bfseries{The native format\textquotesingle{}s own scope is very small.}} Only three files in the entire circuit library use {\ttfamily kind\+: subcirc}\+: {\ttfamily CNTR3.\+yml}, {\ttfamily CNTR4.\+yml}, and {\ttfamily JKFF.\+yml} — and none of them use bit-\/slices in their gate {\ttfamily in\+Prts\+:}, only whole-\/node references. So this work has {\bfseries{zero observable effect on any circuit that exists today}}; it\textquotesingle{}s forward-\/looking correctness work for a code path that\textquotesingle{}s real and reachable ({\ttfamily in\+Port2\+Indxs}\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily .segmented} case, {\ttfamily \doxylink{CircuitIO_8swift}{Circuit\+IO.\+swift}\+:62-\/102}) but currently dead.
\end{DoxyItemize}

What was implemented, in {\ttfamily \doxylink{CircuitIO_8swift}{Circuit\+IO.\+swift}}/{\ttfamily \doxylink{Node_8swift}{Node.\+swift}}/{\ttfamily \doxylink{Circuit_8swift}{Circuit.\+swift}}\+:


\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item {\ttfamily Nod} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Node_8swift}{Node.\+swift}}) gained a real {\ttfamily kind\+: Nd\+Kind} field (default {\ttfamily .simple}), reviving the previously-\/dead {\ttfamily Nd\+Kind} enum ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Circuit_8swift}{Circuit.\+swift}\+:126-\/129}).
\item {\ttfamily add\+Seg}/{\ttfamily circ\+Seg} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{CircuitIO_8swift}{Circuit\+IO.\+swift}}) now tag the slice node they produce {\ttfamily .kind = .slice}, and — two latent bugs found while touching this code — now correctly set that node\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily node\+Drvr} and its source node\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily node\+Sinks}, and now register the new node\textquotesingle{}s name in {\ttfamily circuit.\+node\+LU}. Previously neither the driver/sink edges nor the {\ttfamily node\+LU} entry were set at all\+: since {\ttfamily initialize\+Cmp\+Cnts} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Circuit_8swift}{Circuit.\+swift}\+:558-\/561}) skips ref-\/counting through a node whose driver is {\ttfamily .none}, nothing reading a slice node was ever told it must wait for the {\ttfamily .seg} gate that produces it; and since {\ttfamily Gate.\+eval()}\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily .seg}/{\ttfamily .join} cases write their output via the name-\/based {\ttfamily circuit.\+set\+Node(name\+:...)}, a node missing from {\ttfamily node\+LU} would silently fail to update at all ({\ttfamily set\+Node} prints a warning and no-\/ops on an unknown name) — the slice/join node\textquotesingle{}s value would have stuck at its initial {\ttfamily 0} forever. Both were genuine, if currently unexercised, correctness hazards, caught by the new tests below.
\item A new helper, {\ttfamily add\+Join(seg\+Indices\+:circuit\+:)}, synthesizes a real {\ttfamily .join} gate plus a {\ttfamily .simple}-\/kind output node whenever {\ttfamily in\+Port2\+Indxs}\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily .segmented} case sees ≥2 segments that need concatenating — the output node\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily nbits} is the sum of the inputs\textquotesingle{} {\ttfamily nbits} by construction, satisfying point 5 of the algorithm, and it registers the output node in {\ttfamily node\+LU} the same way. {\ttfamily .bus}\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily .bit}/{\ttfamily .slc} sub-\/cases were left unchanged\+: each element there already maps 1\+:1 to one input slot of the {\itshape enclosing} gate (this is exactly how {\ttfamily .join}-\/kind gates like {\ttfamily CNTR3}\textquotesingle{}s already declare real concatenation, e.\+g. {\ttfamily in\+Prts\+: \mbox{[}Q2, Q1, Q0\mbox{]}}), so no gate-\/insertion logic was needed there.
\item No changes were needed to {\ttfamily \doxylink{Circuit_8swift}{Circuit.\+swift}}\textquotesingle{}s Kahn\textquotesingle{}s-\/algorithm sort — a gate appended to {\ttfamily circuit.\+a\+Circs} with correct {\ttfamily node\+Drvr}/{\ttfamily node\+Sinks} is picked up generically by {\ttfamily make\+Cmp\+Refs}/{\ttfamily initialize\+Cmp\+Cnts}, exactly like any other gate.
\item A third, more serious bug was found once the above made it possible to actually exercise a {\ttfamily .seg} gate for the first time\+: {\ttfamily Gate.\+eval()}\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily .seg} case ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Gate_8swift}{Gate.\+swift}}) never read {\ttfamily self.\+seg} (the stored {\ttfamily (msb, lsb)} range) at all — it looped over the {\itshape source} node\textquotesingle{}s full bit width and rebuilt the output by reading bits {\ttfamily 0, 1, 2, ...} in order, which bit-\/\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}reverses\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*} the entire source value rather than extracting {\ttfamily \mbox{[}msb\+:lsb\mbox{]}}. A {\ttfamily .seg} gate never actually sliced anything. {\bfseries{Fixed}}\+: it now computes {\ttfamily nd.\+sel\+Bits(n1\+: msb, n2\+: lsb).value}, reusing the same correct, already-\/used-\/elsewhere {\ttfamily Two\+Cmplt.\+sel\+Bits} helper ({\ttfamily Shared\+Types/ \doxylink{TwoCmplt_8swift}{Two\+Cmplt.\+swift}\+:241-\/248}) that {\ttfamily \doxylink{Sim_8swift}{Sim.\+swift}}\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily extract\+Slice} also uses. This bug was caught by a test with a genuine partial, asymmetric slice — a full-\/width "{}slice"{} (the only kind exercised while first writing this code) can\textquotesingle{}t distinguish a reversal from a correct extraction, since reversing all of a node\textquotesingle{}s bits and extracting all of a node\textquotesingle{}s bits differ only when the requested range is a strict subset.
\end{DoxyItemize}

{\ttfamily Port\+Def.\+sgmnts}/{\ttfamily resolve\+Circ\+Port}\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily .segmented} case — sub-\/circuit {\itshape boundary} port wiring, a different layer from gate-\/level {\ttfamily in\+Prts\+:} — was left untouched in this pass; it was already confirmed dead in Part 1\textquotesingle{}s investigation. (It was deleted in a later cleanup pass — see "{}\+Later cleanup pass"{} below.)\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md24}{}\doxysection{\texorpdfstring{Verification}{Verification}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md24}
New tests were added under {\ttfamily Tests/\+Twos\+Cmplt\+Tests/} covering\+:
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item The consolidated {\ttfamily Assgn\+AST} shape being produced consistently by all three of its construction call sites (continuous assign, procedural single-\/assign, procedural concat-\/assign).
\item {\ttfamily gen\+Assign\+Stmt} now correctly emitting code for a bit-\/select lvalue (previously silently dropped).
\item The tree-\/walking {\ttfamily .select} evaluator now agreeing with the VM path for the same slice read (previously returned {\ttfamily -\/1}).
\item A {\ttfamily CNTR3}/{\ttfamily CNTR4} regression check (the only current users of the native-\/format {\ttfamily .join} gate) confirming the Logic\+Lib YAML cleanup changed no simulated behavior.
\item Synthetic (no real circuit exercises this path) coverage of {\ttfamily add\+Seg}\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily .slice} tagging and {\ttfamily node\+Drvr}/{\ttfamily node\+Sinks} wiring, and of {\ttfamily in\+Port2\+Indxs}\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily .segmented} case under Option B\+: one segment wires directly with no new gate, two or more produce exactly one {\ttfamily .join} gate whose output is {\ttfamily .simple}-\/kind, correctly-\/sized, and evaluates to the correct concatenation.
\item A regression check that {\ttfamily CNTR3}/{\ttfamily CNTR4}/{\ttfamily JKFF} — the only native-\/format circuits — still load and simulate identically.
\item {\ttfamily test\+Gen\+Concat\+Stmt\+Writes\+All\+Parts}, exercising the fixed {\ttfamily gen\+Concat\+Stmt} end-\/to-\/end against a synthetic {\ttfamily Concat\+Stmnt\+AST} (no production circuit uses {\ttfamily kind\+: concatst} today).
\end{DoxyItemize}\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md25}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Later cleanup pass}{Later cleanup pass}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md25}
Alongside the above, several small, independently-\/diagnosed items were resolved with no known live-\/production impact\+:
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item {\ttfamily assign\+To\+LValue}/{\ttfamily set\+Left\+Net} duplication reduced to one shared helper ({\ttfamily apply\+Slice\+Write}), as described above.
\item {\ttfamily gen\+Concat\+Stmt}\textquotesingle{}s stack-\/discipline bug fixed, as described above.
\item {\ttfamily Port\+Def.\+sgmnts} and {\ttfamily resolve\+Circ\+Port}\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily .segmented} case ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Circuit_8swift}{Circuit.\+swift}}) deleted — confirmed dead (written, never read), and the {\ttfamily Port\+Def} it used to produce ({\ttfamily node\+: "{}"{}, nbits\+: 0, extl\+Indx\+: -\/1}) was never a usable value in the first place. Segmented sub-\/circuit-\/boundary port connections now fail loudly ({\ttfamily precondition\+Failure}) instead of silently producing an inert {\ttfamily Port\+Def}.
\item {\ttfamily set\+Out\+Nd} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Circuit_8swift}{Circuit.\+swift}}) deleted — confirmed zero callers anywhere in the codebase. It mutated a local copy of a {\ttfamily Nod} read from {\ttfamily circ.\+parent!.nodes\mbox{[}...\mbox{]}} and never wrote it back (a classic Swift value-\/type bug), and called {\ttfamily save\+Chng} with the wrong circuit reference; neither defect had any effect since nothing ever called it. The actually-\/ used output-\/propagation path is {\ttfamily Circuit.\+eval}\textquotesingle{}s own {\ttfamily self.\+parent!.set\+Node}/{\ttfamily set\+Node\+Bit} calls, which are correct and untouched.
\item {\ttfamily Sources/\+Twos\+Cmplt/\+Compose} deleted (see above).
\end{DoxyItemize}\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md26}{}\doxysection{\texorpdfstring{Part 4 — Kahn\textquotesingle{}s-\/order scheduling for continuous assigns}{Part 4 — Kahn's-order scheduling for continuous assigns}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md26}
Gate/instance scheduling ({\ttfamily kind\+: instance}/{\ttfamily subcircblck}/{\ttfamily asyncblck}/ {\ttfamily syncblck} entries inside a {\ttfamily kind\+: verilog} module) already used Kahn\textquotesingle{}s algorithm — {\ttfamily Circ\+Def.\+to\+Circuit()} wires each instance\textquotesingle{}s ports and {\ttfamily make\+Cmp\+Refs}/{\ttfamily initialize\+Cmp\+Cnts}/{\ttfamily sort\+Cmp\+Refs} build a real topological {\ttfamily eval\+Order} across sibling instances. Continuous {\ttfamily assign} statements did not\+: they were compiled to bytecode ({\ttfamily Circ\+Def.\+assgn\+Blcks}) and run unconditionally, in raw declaration order, every timestep ({\ttfamily run\+All\+Assign\+Blcks}) — with no dependency ordering, and no relationship to the {\ttfamily eval\+Order} scheduler at all.\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md27}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{What changed}{What changed}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md27}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item {\ttfamily Nod}/{\ttfamily Circuit} gained no new per-\/node representation, but {\ttfamily Circuit} gained {\ttfamily assgn\+Blk\+Writes\+: \mbox{[}\mbox{[}Int\mbox{]}\mbox{]}}/{\ttfamily assgn\+Blk\+Reads\+: \mbox{[}\mbox{[}Int\mbox{]}\mbox{]}} — one entry per continuous-\/assign block, recording which nodes it writes and reads.
\item {\ttfamily Cmp\+Type} gained a {\ttfamily .assgn\+Blk} case. {\ttfamily make\+Cmp\+Refs}, {\ttfamily get\+Out\+Refs}, and the {\ttfamily shw\+\_\+ordr} debug helper ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Utilities_8swift}{Utilities.\+swift}}) were updated for it.
\item Two new pure functions in {\ttfamily \doxylink{Compile_8swift}{Compile.\+swift}}\+: {\ttfamily lvalue\+Base\+Names(\+\_\+\+:)} (like the existing {\ttfamily lvalue\+Base\+Name}, but decomposes a {\ttfamily .concat} lvalue into every node it writes instead of collapsing it to a placeholder) and {\ttfamily referenced\+Node\+Names(\+\_\+\+:in\+:)} (walks an {\ttfamily Expr} tree via {\ttfamily Expr\+Id}s, collecting every {\ttfamily .node}/{\ttfamily .select} name referenced, recursing through {\ttfamily .binary}/{\ttfamily .unary}/{\ttfamily .gate}/{\ttfamily .cndtn}/{\ttfamily .syscall}/{\ttfamily .concat} args).
\item {\ttfamily Circ\+Def.\+to\+Circuit()} now has a wiring step, right after the existing instance-\/wiring loop and before {\ttfamily gate\+Slots()}, that walks {\ttfamily self.\+behav}\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily .assgnblck} entries (not {\ttfamily circ\+Def.\+assgn\+Blcks}, which isn\textquotesingle{}t populated until {\ttfamily self.\+Compile(circ)} runs later in the same function — a sequencing constraint that had to be worked around, not reordered, since {\ttfamily Compile()} also populates {\ttfamily always\+States}/{\ttfamily init\+States}), computes each one\textquotesingle{}s write/read node sets via the two functions above, and wires {\ttfamily node\+Drvr}/{\ttfamily node\+Sinks} exactly like the existing {\ttfamily a\+Circs}-\/wiring loop does for ordinary gates. The {\ttfamily .assgn\+Blk} index assigned is "{}the Nth   \`{}.\+assgnblck\`{} encountered in \`{}self.\+behav\`{}"{} — confirmed to match {\ttfamily copy\+Behav()}\textquotesingle{}s later population of {\ttfamily circ\+Def.\+assgn\+Blcks} (a simple append-\/in-\/encounter-\/order, always correct regardless of interleaving with other behav-\/block kinds).
\item {\ttfamily run\+All\+Assign\+Blcks} was replaced by {\ttfamily run\+Assign\+Blck(\+\_\+\+:ctx\+:)}, which runs one indexed assign block\textquotesingle{}s compiled code. {\ttfamily Circuit.\+eval()}\textquotesingle{}s two {\ttfamily eval\+Order} dispatch loops gained a {\ttfamily .assgn\+Blk} case\+: the async branch calls {\ttfamily run\+Assign\+Blck}; the sync branch is a no-\/op (continuous assigns are combinational, like {\ttfamily .a\+Circ}, not re-\/evaluated on the sync pass). The four old unconditional call sites ({\ttfamily eval()} before the dispatch loop, {\ttfamily eval()} again after always-\/blocks fire, {\ttfamily sim\+Vrlg\+Inits}, and a presumed-\/dead call in {\ttfamily sim\+Vrlg\+Alwys}) were all removed.
\end{DoxyItemize}\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md28}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{A dormant, separate bug found along the way}{A dormant, separate bug found along the way}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md28}
{\ttfamily generate\+All\+Blcks} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Compile_8swift}{Compile.\+swift}}) computes a {\ttfamily type\+Idx} for writing compiled bytecode into {\ttfamily circ\+Def.\+assgn\+Blcks}/{\ttfamily init\+Blcks}/{\ttfamily always\+Blcks} by tracking {\itshape consecutive runs} of the same behav-\/block kind, not an overall per-\/kind counter — it resets to 0 whenever the kind changes. If a module\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily behav\+\_\+blcks} ever interleaved, say, {\ttfamily assign, instance, assign, assign}, the second and third assigns would both compute {\ttfamily type\+Idx == 0}/{\ttfamily 1} starting from the interleaved reset rather than continuing from the first assign\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily type\+Idx}, misassigning compiled code into the wrong {\ttfamily assgn\+Blcks\mbox{[}i\mbox{]}} slot. Checked all 203 {\ttfamily assign}-\/containing files in {\ttfamily Resources/\+Circuit\+Lib}\+: every one has at most two contiguous groups of behav-\/block kinds (e.\+g. all instances then all assigns, or pure-\/assign-\/only) — never true interleaving — so this is real but currently dormant. Not fixed here (orthogonal to scheduling order); the new {\ttfamily .assgn\+Blk} wiring avoids inheriting it by counting assign blocks the simple, always-\/correct way {\ttfamily copy\+Behav()} does, not by copying {\ttfamily type\+Idx}\textquotesingle{}s logic.\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md29}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{The reactivity question, and why always-\/block-\/driven nodes need no special case}{The reactivity question, and why always-block-driven nodes need no special case}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md29}
Continuous assigns are meant to react immediately to any input change, including one an always-\/block just made in the same timestep. The old "{}run every assign again after always-\/blocks fire"{} call existed to approximate this. Kahn\textquotesingle{}s-\/order dispatch has no equivalent mechanism — each component runs once, at its sorted position — so simply deleting that second run risked silently dropping reactivity for an assign depending on an always-\/block\textquotesingle{}s output.

It turns out no special-\/casing was needed\+: a node is only ever given a structural {\ttfamily node\+Drvr} during build-\/time wiring (native gates, instance ports, {\ttfamily add\+Seg}/{\ttfamily add\+Join}, and now assign blocks) — {\ttfamily set\+Node}, which is what an always-\/block\textquotesingle{}s procedural writes go through at simulation time, never sets {\ttfamily node\+Drvr}. So a node written only by an always-\/block already has {\ttfamily node\+Drvr == .none}, and {\ttfamily initialize\+Cmp\+Cnts} already skips creating a dependency edge for {\ttfamily .none}-\/driven nodes (the same skip it already applies to {\ttfamily .i\+Prt}-\/ and sync-\/driven nodes). An assign reading such a node simply isn\textquotesingle{}t blocked by it — it runs at its own Kahn-\/sorted position and reads whatever value is currently there, "{}stale until next trigger,"{} exactly matching how sync/register dependencies are already treated elsewhere. This is a deliberate, user-\/confirmed semantic choice, not an accident of the implementation.

{\bfseries{Update (Twos\+Cmplt {\ttfamily b857af8}, 2026-\/10-\/28)\+: assigns are re-\/run after always blocks again.}} "{}\+Stale until next trigger"{} left a latch\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily assign QP = STR} ({\ttfamily STR \texorpdfstring{$<$}{<}= \#d D} in an always block) following {\ttfamily STR} only at the cell\textquotesingle{}s next input event\+: TST\+\_\+\+LTCHR\+\_\+4\+X1\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily QP} changed half a period late. So {\ttfamily Circuit.\+eval} now, after the always blocks run, re-\/runs the module\textquotesingle{}s assigns in {\ttfamily eval\+Order} while that changes something, and the always blocks woken by those changes, at most {\ttfamily loop\+Iter\+Cap} times ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Circuit_8swift}{Circuit.\+swift}}, the always-\/block section of {\ttfamily eval}). The ordering described above is unchanged. Current description\+: {\ttfamily SIMULATION\+\_\+\+ALGORITHM.\+md} §7.3, step 3.\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md30}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Verified regression-\/free}{Verified regression-free}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md30}
{\ttfamily MULT\+\_\+25\+P125.\+yml} ({\ttfamily Resources/\+Circuit\+Lib}) has three real continuous assigns with a genuine dependency — {\ttfamily OUT} reads {\ttfamily sum}, which an earlier assign writes. Confirmed via {\ttfamily Assign\+Scheduling\+Tests.\+test\+Real\+Circuit\+Assigns\+Scheduled\+In\+Dependency\+Order} that the {\ttfamily sum}-\/writing assign is scheduled before the {\ttfamily OUT}-\/writing one. {\ttfamily TST\+\_\+\+ACCUM3} (which instantiates {\ttfamily M1\+M\+\_\+\+QDACCUM5}, the circuit with the 16-\/bit-\/concat-\/of-\/selects continuous assign cited in Part 1) was run end-\/to-\/end before and after this change (by temporarily stashing the {\ttfamily \doxylink{Circuit_8swift}{Circuit.\+swift}}/{\ttfamily \doxylink{CircDef_8swift}{Circ\+Def.\+swift}} scheduling changes and re-\/running) and produced byte-\/for-\/byte identical results — {\ttfamily QD\+\_\+} ends at value {\ttfamily 0x30000}, {\ttfamily upd\+Tm=12}, in both cases. This is now a permanent regression test, {\ttfamily TSTACCUM3\+Regression\+Test}.

{\ttfamily QD\+\_\+\+DDFS5}/{\ttfamily Sine5} (the circuit behind the still-\/open {\ttfamily FINE\mbox{[}7\+:0\mbox{]}} investigation) has {\bfseries{no}} continuous assigns at all — its entire {\ttfamily COS\+\_\+\+LU5}/{\ttfamily SIN\+\_\+\+LU5} pipeline is built from structural instances — so this phase has no bearing on that investigation either way; confirmed its test output is byte-\/for-\/byte unchanged.\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md31}{}\doxysection{\texorpdfstring{Part 5 — $<$tt$>$\+RL\+\_\+$<$/tt$>$ stuck at 0 in $<$tt$>$\+TST\+\_\+\+ACCUM3$<$/tt$>$\+: multi-\/bit output-\/port slices were never wired correctly}{Part 5 — <tt>RL\_</tt> stuck at 0 in <tt>TST\_ACCUM3</tt>: multi-bit output-port slices were never wired correctly}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md31}
\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md32}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{The bug}{The bug}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md32}
{\ttfamily TST\+\_\+\+ACCUM3} never advanced its accumulator\+: {\ttfamily RL\+\_\+} (an 18-\/bit register, {\ttfamily M1\+M\+\_\+\+QDACCUM5}\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily REG0R}/{\ttfamily KM\+\_\+\+REGS18}) stayed at its reset value {\ttfamily 0} for an entire simulation run, even though its feedback adder ({\ttfamily ADDR0R}, module {\ttfamily CLA18}) received a genuinely nonzero input ({\ttfamily A = FRQ\mbox{[}33\+:16\mbox{]} = 16384} for {\ttfamily FRQ = 0x40000000}). Since {\ttfamily QD\+\_\+} is purely combinational from {\ttfamily RL\+\_\+}, it also appeared frozen — this is what {\ttfamily debug\+\_\+utilities.\+md}/earlier sessions observed as "{}\`{}\+RL\+\_\+\`{} never appears in \`{}chngs.\+out\`{}."{}

Two plausible hypotheses from prior sessions — a wrong {\ttfamily circuit=sync}/ {\ttfamily async} module parameter somewhere in the {\ttfamily M1\+M\+\_\+\+QDACCUM5 → KM\+\_\+\+REGS18 → DG\+\_\+\+DR\+\_\+3\+X2} chain, and the pre-\/existing {\ttfamily .v\+Circ} async/sync dispatch asymmetry in {\ttfamily Circuit.\+eval()} — were both directly checked against the real {\ttfamily Resources/\+Circuit\+Lib/\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}.yml} files and the xschem {\ttfamily .sym} library, and both checked out correct. Runtime tracing (temporarily instrumenting {\ttfamily Circuit.\+eval()}, since removed) then isolated the actual fault\+: {\ttfamily CLA18}\textquotesingle{}s sum output ({\ttfamily S}) stayed {\ttfamily 0} no matter what {\ttfamily A}/{\ttfamily B} were. {\ttfamily CLA18} is a carry-\/lookahead adder built from a hierarchy of smaller adders — {\ttfamily CLA18 → CLA8 + CLA10 → CLA4 → CLA2} — and at every level, two sibling instances each drive a different {\bfseries{slice}} of the parent\textquotesingle{}s own wider {\ttfamily S} bus, e.\+g. ({\ttfamily CLA4.\+yml})\+:


\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{-\/\ \ \ name:\ CLA2\_0}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ module:\ CLA2}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ ports:}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ -\/\ ...}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ -\/\ \ \ port:\ None}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ node:\ \{\ kind:\ slice,\ name:\ S,\ sgmnts:\ [1,\ 0]\ \}\ \ \ \#\ drives\ S[1:0]}
\DoxyCodeLine{-\/\ \ \ name:\ CLA2\_1}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ module:\ CLA2}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ ports:}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ -\/\ ...}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ -\/\ \ \ port:\ None}
\DoxyCodeLine{\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ node:\ \{\ kind:\ slice,\ name:\ S,\ sgmnts:\ [3,\ 2]\ \}\ \ \ \#\ drives\ S[3:2]}

\end{DoxyCode}


An isolated test confirmed the leaf-\/level {\ttfamily CLA2} instances themselves compute correctly (e.\+g. given {\ttfamily A=1}, correctly output {\ttfamily S=1}), but that correct value never survived being written back into the parent\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily S} node. The cause was in the output-\/port wiring in {\ttfamily Circ\+Def.\+to\+Circuit()} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{CircDef_8swift}{Circ\+Def.\+swift}}, the {\ttfamily is\+Output} branch of the instance-\/port-\/wiring loop)\+:


\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{cir.oPrts[idx].extlBitIndex\ =\ parseSingleBitIndex(nd\_nm)}

\end{DoxyCode}


{\ttfamily parse\+Single\+Bit\+Index} correctly returns {\ttfamily nil} for a range like {\ttfamily "{}\+S\mbox{[}1\+:0\mbox{]}"{}} (it only recognizes single-\/bit indices like {\ttfamily "{}\+S\mbox{[}3\mbox{]}"{}}) — but {\ttfamily Port\+Def} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Circuit_8swift}{Circuit.\+swift}}) had no representation for a multi-\/bit range at all, only {\ttfamily extl\+Bit\+Index\+: Int?}. So a range connection fell through to the same case as a whole-\/node connection, and the propagation code at the tail of {\ttfamily Circuit.\+eval()} did\+:


\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keyword}{self}.parent!.setNode(prt.node,\ val:\ nd.node.value,\ tm:\ nd.updTm)}

\end{DoxyCode}


— an unmasked, unshifted overwrite of the {\bfseries{entire}} parent {\ttfamily S} node with just this one child\textquotesingle{}s own (unshifted) value. With two siblings each doing this for the same base name ({\ttfamily base\+Name("{}\+S\mbox{[}1\+:0\mbox{]}"{})} and {\ttfamily base\+Name("{}\+S\mbox{[}3\+:2\mbox{]}"{})} both collapse to {\ttfamily "{}\+S"{}}), each eval pass\textquotesingle{}s result was simply clobbered by whichever sibling happened to be evaluated last in {\ttfamily eval\+Order} — not combined, and not bit-\/shifted into its correct position even when it wasn\textquotesingle{}t. This is a distinct, deeper bug than anything Part 1-\/4 touched\+: those phases were explicitly scoped to the {\itshape native} ({\ttfamily kind\+: subcirc}) format\textquotesingle{}s slice/join handling; this is the analogous gap in the {\itshape Verilog-\/derived} ({\ttfamily kind\+: verilog}) format\textquotesingle{}s instance {\bfseries{output}}-\/port wiring — input-\/side slice extraction ({\ttfamily Circuit.\+eval()}\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily i\+Prts} handling) was already correct and unaffected.\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md33}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{The fix}{The fix}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md33}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item {\ttfamily Port\+Def} ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Circuit_8swift}{Circuit.\+swift}}) gained {\ttfamily extl\+Bit\+Range\+: (msb\+: Int, lsb\+: Int)?}, alongside the existing single-\/bit {\ttfamily extl\+Bit\+Index\+: Int?}.
\item A new {\ttfamily parse\+Bit\+Range(\+\_\+\+:)} helper ({\ttfamily \doxylink{Utilities_8swift}{Utilities.\+swift}}, next to {\ttfamily parse\+Single\+Bit\+Index}) parses {\ttfamily "{}\+S\mbox{[}3\+:2\mbox{]}"{}}-\/style ranges.
\item {\ttfamily Circ\+Def.\+to\+Circuit()}\textquotesingle{}s output-\/port wiring now tries {\ttfamily parse\+Bit\+Range} first, falling back to {\ttfamily parse\+Single\+Bit\+Index} for true single-\/bit connections.
\item A new {\ttfamily Circuit.\+set\+Node\+Bits(\+\_\+\+:msb\+:lsb\+:val\+:tm\+:)} (mirroring the existing {\ttfamily set\+Node\+Bit}) merges a value into a bit range of a node, preserving the node\textquotesingle{}s other bits — the multi-\/bit counterpart of {\ttfamily set\+Node\+Bit}.
\item {\ttfamily Circuit.\+eval()}\textquotesingle{}s tail-\/of-\/function output-\/port propagation now checks {\ttfamily extl\+Bit\+Range} first, then {\ttfamily extl\+Bit\+Index}, then falls back to a full {\ttfamily set\+Node} overwrite (unchanged for genuinely whole-\/node connections).
\end{DoxyItemize}\hypertarget{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md34}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Verification}{Verification}}\label{md_Sources_2TwosCmplt_2TwosCmplt_8docc_2CircDef_autotoc_md34}

\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item {\ttfamily CLA18\+Isolation\+Test} (new, permanent)\+: loads {\ttfamily CLA18} directly via {\ttfamily gen\+Circ}, drives {\ttfamily A=16384, B=0, CI=0}, and asserts {\ttfamily S == 16384} — fails against the old code, passes after the fix.
\item {\ttfamily TSTACCUM3\+Regression\+Test} (updated)\+: its old expected values ({\ttfamily QD\+\_\+ == 0x30000} at {\ttfamily upd\+Tm=12}) described the {\itshape bug}, not correct behavior, and needed updating. After the fix, {\ttfamily RL\+\_\+} genuinely updates throughout the run (asserted via {\ttfamily rl.\+upd\+Tm \texorpdfstring{$>$}{>} 0}). {\ttfamily QD\+\_\+}\textquotesingle{}s final value is still {\ttfamily 0x30000}, but now at {\ttfamily upd\+Tm=128011} (continuously updating, not frozen) — this specific final value is a coincidence of the test\textquotesingle{}s own parameters ({\ttfamily FRQ=0x40000000} increments {\ttfamily RL\+\_\+} by {\ttfamily 16384} per clock, and {\ttfamily 128 clocks \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*} 16384 = 2\texorpdfstring{$^\wedge$}{\string^}21}, an exact multiple of {\ttfamily RL\+\_\+}\textquotesingle{}s width {\ttfamily 2\texorpdfstring{$^\wedge$}{\string^}18}, so {\ttfamily RL\+\_\+} wraps back to exactly {\ttfamily 0} right at this run\textquotesingle{}s finish time), not evidence the bug is still present.
\item Full {\ttfamily swift test}\+: all pass except the pre-\/existing, unrelated {\ttfamily QDDFS5\+Fine\+Mltply\+Tests} failure (that circuit\textquotesingle{}s {\ttfamily Sine5}/{\ttfamily COS\+\_\+\+LU5} stuck-\/ at-\/zero issue does not involve multi-\/bit output-\/port slices anywhere in its own structure, and this fix did not change its behavior).
\item The {\ttfamily .v\+Circ} async/sync dispatch asymmetry documented in earlier investigation notes is still real (the {\ttfamily async == true} branch still ignores a child\textquotesingle{}s own {\ttfamily circ.\+sync}), but is now confirmed {\bfseries{not}} to be the cause of this bug — left as-\/is, no fix attempted, since it wasn\textquotesingle{}t shown to cause any observed incorrect behavior. 
\end{DoxyItemize}
